headline: High-risk filesystem and orchestration overlap: AutoGPT can write via shell/filesystem while Kestra can write, egress broadly, and trigger external actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and Kestra exposes files plus stdin/stdout and many task outputs. A plausible bridge exists if Kestra feeds AutoGPT-generated artifacts back as instructions, but no direct shared channel is documented. This is interaction-based and uncertain, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Kestra passes AutoGPT-produced files or logs into a task that interprets them as instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace or mounted storage
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable automatic parsing of generated files as prompts
Add a provenance header check before any file-to-prompt handoff
Use read-only mounts for AutoGPT inputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the orchestration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; Kestra reads/writes workflow data, logs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data, with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or data class, sensitive material can flow from one into the other and out over network paths. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default-style deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem or storage bucket
IF Kestra tasks forward logs, artifacts, or inputs containing sensitive data to AutoGPT
IF AutoGPT is configured to send retrieved file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate storage roots
Mask secrets in logs and artifacts before handoff
Disable egress for any task handling sensitive data
Review shared OAuth or cloud credentials before deployment
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention at the workflow boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell and spawn subprocesses, and Kestra can write files while AutoGPT can use the filesystem. Kestra also supports multiple instances, but AutoGPT does not, so concurrent mutation of shared state is a realistic conflict path. With no locking or isolation documented, the overlap can corrupt files or workflow state in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, repo, or storage volume
IF Kestra schedules parallel tasks that mutate shared files
IF AutoGPT writes intermediate state while Kestra rewrites the same artifacts
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable parallel mutation of shared artifacts
Snapshot shared state before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can trigger emails, Slack, PagerDuty, cloud, and database actions, so if it consumes AutoGPT output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into real-world actions. AutoGPT can generate unverified plans or facts, and Kestra’s declarative workflows may execute them without a human verification step. That makes the pair dangerous by default unless explicit validation is added.
conditions: IF Kestra uses AutoGPT output as an input to action tasks
IF no validation step checks AutoGPT outputs before execution
IF workflows can send notifications or modify cloud/database resources
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before action tasks
Validate AutoGPT outputs against a schema
Require dry-run mode for first executions
Log and diff proposed actions before commit
requires-engineering: add policy checks for downstream side effects

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while AutoGPT can access files and egress to external services. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because the data classes and external channels are broad, the safest supported rating is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Kestra workflows
IF AutoGPT sends any of those data classes to external APIs
IF residency or retention requirements apply to the shared data
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent
Block regulated data from external egress paths
Set retention limits on logs and artifacts
Document residency for each workflow
requires-engineering: align both agents to the same compliance boundary
